verses.1: And the Angel of the LORD ascended from the cloud to the people and said, “I will bring you out of Egypt. I will take you to the land that I promised your ancestors. I will make a covenant with you forever.”
verses.2: And you shall not make a covenant with the inhabitants of this land, who worship their idols. And you shall not hear what I say. What have you done?
verses.3: And I also said that I would not let them go from your side. They shall be your neighbors, and they shall be your friends.
verses.4: And when the Lord spoke these words to all the children of Israel, the people cried out in praise and worship.
verses.5: And they called out the name of that place. They went there and worshipped Jehovah there.
verses.6: And Joshua sent the people away. The sons of Israel went away, each to their own land, to take possession of the land.
verses.7: And the people obeyed Jehovah throughout all the days of Joshua. They also obeyed during all the days of the elders who lived after Joshua’s time. These elders saw all the great deeds that Jehovah did for Israel.
verses.8: And Joshua ben Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of one hundred and ten years old.
verses.9: And they buried him in the territory of his inheritance, at Timnat-Herodes, on Mount Ephraim, from Tsafon to Mount Gaash.
verses.10: And all those generations were gathered together before their fathers. Then another generation arose after them, who did not know Jehovah, nor knew what He had done to Israel.
verses.11: And the children of Israel did what was evil in the eyes of Jehovah, and they served their gods.
verses.12: And they abandoned Jehovah, the God of their ancestors who brought them out of Egypt. They went after other gods, those of the nations around them. They worshiped those gods instead of Jehovah, and they became angry with Jehovah.
verses.13: And they abandoned Jehovah and worshipped the gods of other nations.
verses.14: And Jehovah struck Israel, and He handed them over to their enemies. They were sold into slavery by their own people around them. They could no longer stand before their enemies.
verses.15: In everything that the hand of Jehovah did, it was for their harm. Just as Jehovah spoke, and when Jehovah blessed them, He created many things for them.
verses.16: And Jehovah raised up judges to save them from their oppressors.
verses.17: And even their judges did not listen to them, because they worshiped other gods instead of God. They turned away from the path their ancestors had followed—that is, to obey the commands of Jehovah. They never did so.
verses.18: And when Jehovah established judges for them, then Jehovah would be with those judges and save them from their enemies. For all the time of their judgment, Jehovah would comfort them from their hardships and sufferings.
verses.19: And in that day, those who were wicked will be seated and will destroy their ancestors. They will go after other gods to worship them and bow down before them. They will not leave their evil ways or their difficult paths behind.
verses.20: And Jehovah struck Israel, saying, “Because this people have broken my covenant that I made with their ancestors. They did not listen to my voice.”
verses.21: Nor do I want to continue to mention any of those people from other nations who were left behind after Joshua died.
verses.22: So that they may test Israel. They must keep the way of the LORD as their path, just as their ancestors did. Otherwise…
verses.23: And Jehovah handed these nations over to them, so that they could not be destroyed quickly, and they were not given into the hands of Joshua.
